status_summary: No proposal to eliminate Head Start or the Office of Head Start was found as of 2026-10-07. The program was funded at $12.357 billion in the fiscal year 2026 appropriation signed 2026-02-03 as Public Law 119-75 (an $85 million increase, per an advocacy group's tracker), and HHS's fiscal year 2027 congressional justification requests the same amount while proposing to let state standards apply to Head Start programs. The Mandate's fallback is met: ACF removed the masking requirement in January 2023 and the vaccination and testing requirements in June 2023, before this administration, and a direct final rule published 2025-12-19 (effective 2026-02-17 absent significant adverse comments; no withdrawal appears in the Federal Register) removed the remaining COVID-19 mitigation policy requirement. ACF has also proposed to drop Performance Standards wage and benefit requirements (2026-05-12) and to rescind and replace the 2024 Performance Standards (2026-08-07; comments closed 2026-10-06), and HHS's July 2025 notice treating Head Start as a federal public benefit was set aside by a 2026-09-21 summary judgment ruling in a suit by 20 states and D.C.

timeline.event: HHS publishes a revised PRWORA interpretation, effective immediately, listing Head Start (and Title X, among others) as a federal public benefit.
A federal court in Rhode Island preliminarily enjoins the agencies' July 2025 PRWORA notices in a suit by 20 states and D.C. (date and scope per a school-board association legal update).

ACF publishes a direct final rule (90 FR 59397) removing the requirement that Head Start programs maintain a COVID-19 mitigation policy, effective 2026-02-17 absent significant adverse comment; the rule's background states the masking requirement was removed 2023-01-06 and the vaccine and testing requirements 2023-06-26.

The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148) is approved as Public Law 119-75, with the fiscal year 2026 Labor-HHS appropriation as Division B; First Focus on Children's tracker lists Head Start at $12.357 billion, an $85 million increase.

HHS's fiscal year 2027 request (release date of the Budget in Brief used for this entry) sets Head Start at $12,356,820,000, the same as fiscal year 2026 enacted, and proposes allowing state standards on licensing, health and safety, ratios and quality to apply to Head Start; the justification also describes integrating ACF and the Administration for Community Living under a new Administration for Children, Families, and Communities.
ACF proposes removing Performance Standards requirements on wages and benefits, estimating savings of over $2 billion for Head Start programs.

ACF proposes to rescind and replace the 2024 Head Start Program Performance Standards (91 FR 51248), estimating about $2.2 billion in annual impacts at full implementation in 2031 that could fund additional slots; the proposal states the Head Start Act's requirements remain in effect. Comments closed 2026-10-06.

In State of New York v. U.S. Department of Justice (D.R.I., No. 1:25-cv-00345), the court grants summary judgment to 20 states and D.C., vacating the July 2025 PRWORA notices of DOJ, HHS and three other departments (HHS's as procedurally invalid for lacking notice-and-comment rulemaking) and enjoining their enforcement against the plaintiffs; the order does not mention Head Start.

title: Eliminate the Head Start program and the Office of Head Start
uncertainties: The fiscal year 2027 Head Start figures come from an excerpt of HHS's congressional justification whose Head Start section was cut off, and the entry date is the Budget in Brief release date reported by a law firm, not a date printed on the justification. The fiscal year 2026 signing date and funding level come from an advocacy group's tracker (the Senate Appropriations Committee's conference summary also lists $12.4 billion, an $85 million increase over fiscal year 2025). The 2025-09-10 injunction date comes from a school-board association post that does not name the case; a Hogan Lovells article reports a separate Washington district court injunction against enforcing the HHS notice as to Head Start, which was not verified. The 2026-09-21 order does not mention Head Start and whether HHS appealed it is unknown. Not verified: changes to Office of Head Start staffing or regional offices, and the later sections of the proposed rules. Federal Register queries for Head Start documents from 2025-12-01 through 2026-10-07 and budget documents showed no elimination proposal. Re-check on 2026-10-15: GovInfo confirms Public Law 119-75 (H.R. 7148) is the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 dated 2026-02-03 with a Labor, HHS and Education division, but the reader truncated its text before the Head Start line, so the 12.357 billion dollar figure still rests on the advocacy tracker. Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, 2026-01-23) is the Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (Divisions A to C), not Labor-HHS. A Federal Register search for 'Head Start' from 2026-09-15 returned only an unrelated Title IX rule, and two web searches found no HHS reorganization affecting the Office of Head Start after 2026-09-21 (results were 2025 regional office closure items).
